William Graham, president of the Board of Trade, in addressing a dinner of the British Chambers of Commerce last night, said that the feeling was general that the bottom of the business depression had not been reached, but that none should give way to pessimism or despair. Mr. Graham said that the country again was on the verge of reaching the dismal point where there were 1,500.000 men out of work. He blamed the great slump in commodity prices, which promoted uncertainty and extreme timidity about buying and manufacturing. 1
